_what_this_is: A template. Copy it to data/sample_pairs/pairs.json, put your audio in
data/sample_pairs/audio/, and fill in one entry per pair: an original record, the
song that sampled it, and what you know about the flip. Everything under data/ is
gitignored, so neither the audio nor this file leaves your machine.
Run it with: python scripts/eval_accuracy.py --dataset sample_pairs --no-gate

_fields.id: your name for the pair. It DOES appear in the shared scores file, so use a codename if the title should stay private.
_fields.original: required. The record that was sampled, as a filename in audio_dir (the suffix is optional).
_fields.song: optional. The finished song that used it. Needed only for tempo_ratio and pitch_shift.
_fields.flip: where in the ORIGINAL the loop came from. '1:04' | '1:04-1:12' | [64, 72] | {from, to} | {at, length_s} | {at, bars, source_bpm}. A bare timestamp is enough.
_fields.tolerance_s: optional. How far off your timestamp might be (default 1 s). Widen it when you are guessing.
_fields.tempo_ratio: optional. Song tempo / record tempo: 1.08 means sped up 8 %. Or give original_bpm and song_bpm and it is worked out.
_fields.pitch_semitones: optional. How far the sample was pitched, in semitones: '+2', -5. pitch_cents works too.
_fields.original_bpm: optional. The record's own BPM, as you know it. Also scores the ordinary tempo metrics.
_fields.original_key: optional. The record's key ('Bbm', 'F minor'). Also scores the ordinary key metrics.
_fields.filtered: optional, free text. What was removed or filtered: 'low-passed, drums gone'. Recorded, not scored (yet).
_fields.notes: optional, free text. Stays on your machine; never written to the results file.
